title: Sentence Improvement
intro: Sentence improvement underlines a part of a sentence and asks for the best replacement (or 'no improvement'). It is error spotting plus a fix: you must both find what is wrong and choose the correct, natural rewrite. The same rule set applies, and the winning answer is the grammatically correct option that changes the least.

items.name: Fix the rule
items.formula: identify the exact grammar error first

items.name: Minimal change
items.formula: prefer the correct option closest to the original

items.name: Keep the meaning
items.formula: the replacement must not change the sense

items.name: "No improvement"
items.formula: a real option — use it when the original is correct

topics.name: Subject–Verb Agreement
topics.details: Match the verb to the true subject. Singular subjects (each, every, one of) take singular verbs; 'a number of' takes plural. Two subjects with 'and' are plural; with 'or/nor' the verb agrees with the nearer subject.

solved.problem: Improve: "One of my friends are a doctor."
Improve: "The team are playing well." (as a unit)
Improve: "Neither the teacher nor the students was present."
Improve: "A number of people was waiting."

unsolved.problem: Improve: "Each of the answers are correct."
Improve: "Either of the two roads lead there."
Improve: "He, as well as his friends, were late."
Improve: "Ten kilometres are a long way."

topics.name: Tense Correction
topics.details: Keep tenses consistent and matched to time markers. After 'since/for' use the perfect; in conditionals match the pattern; reported speech shifts the tense back; the earlier of two past actions takes the past perfect.

solved.problem: Improve: "When I reached, the train already left."
solved.solution: "already left" → "had already left" (past perfect for the earlier action).

solved.problem: Improve: "If I was you, I would accept it."
Improve: "He is working here for five years."
Improve: "I shall meet him after I will finish."

unsolved.problem: Improve: "If it rains, I would stay home."

topics.name: Preposition & Article Fixes
topics.details: Replace a wrong preposition or article with the correct fixed form: 'superior to', 'fond of', 'die of (a disease)', 'on foot'. Insert/remove articles correctly.

unsolved.problem: Improve: "She is married with a lawyer."
Improve: "He goes to the school by foot."

topics.name: Word Order & Redundancy
topics.details: Improve clumsy order and cut redundancy. Adverbs of frequency go before the main verb. Avoid saying the same thing twice: 'return back', 'repeat again', 'free gift', 'final conclusion'.

solved.solution: Remove "free" → "a gift" (a gift is free by definition).

unsolved.problem: Improve: "We reached at the final conclusion."
Improve: "He is a new innovation in the team."

shortcuts: Find the grammar error first, then choose the fix that changes the least.
Match the verb to the TRUE subject (ignore "as well as", "along with" phrases).
Past perfect for the earlier of two past actions.
Learn fixed forms: superior TO, fond OF, on foot, died OF.
Cut redundancy: return back, repeat again, free gift, final conclusion.
mistakes: Picking a fluent-sounding option that introduces a new error.
Ignoring "No improvement" when the original is already correct.
Changing the meaning while fixing the grammar.
Missing redundancy because it "sounds normal" in speech.
pyq: SSC sentence-improvement repeats subject-verb agreement, tense consistency, fixed prepositions and redundancy fixes. Diagnose the rule, then pick the minimal correct rewrite.
summary: Sentence improvement is error spotting plus the correct, minimal fix. Diagnose the rule (agreement, tense, preposition, redundancy), choose the option that corrects it while changing the least and preserving meaning, and remember "No improvement" is a valid answer when the original is right.
